subject: Justin Blinder, Ground Truth: a device that converts census rent-burden data into physical brake resistance on a Citi Bike

S2.name: US Census Bureau ACS margins-of-error training material

S3.name: HUD USER / CRS on the 30 percent cost-burden standard

S4.name: Dezeen (headline/listing only; article body 403 to us)
S4.note: NOT USED as evidence; recorded as the feed item that surfaced the subject

F01.proposition: A device made by the artist Justin Blinder attaches to the front fork of a docked Citi Bike and overrides the front brake to change how hard the bike is to pedal.
F01.support_span: attaches to the front fork of a docked Citi Bike and overrides the front-brake, to adjust pedal resistance

F02.proposition: The device was built from a GPS module, an ESP32S3 microcontroller, a high-torque servo motor, an SD card reader, an OLED display and a custom circuit board, in a 3D-printed enclosure.
F02.support_span: GPS module, ESP32S3 microcontroller, high-torque servo motor, and an SD card reader

F03.proposition: The servo pulls the existing front brake arm along the same axis as the rider's own brake cable; the rider's levers stay functional and always override, and the device can be removed by hand in seconds.
F03.support_span: The mechanism pulls the existing brake arm along the axis its own lever cable uses. The rider's own brake levers remain fully functional and always override.

F04.proposition: The device holds no internet connection and saves no location data; the dataset is stored on an SD card and read locally.
F04.support_span: The device does not connect to the internet or collect data. The dataset it reads is stored on the device.

F05.proposition: The enclosure was modelled from a photogrammetry scan of an electric Citi Bike's front fork and drum brake hub.
F05.support_span: Scan of the electric Citi Bike front fork and drum brake hub, used to model the enclosure.

F06.proposition: The data is the American Community Survey five-year estimates at block-group level, covering 2020 through 2024.
F06.support_span: American Community Survey (ACS) data at the block-group level ... The five-year estimates describe 2020 through 2024.

F07.proposition: Two indicators were blended into one score: the median share of income spent on rent, and the share of renter households spending at least half their income on housing.
F07.support_span: the median share of income spent on rent, and the percentage of renter households spending at least half of their income on housing

F08.proposition: The top quantile was removed from the dataset, because a high-income household may spend heavily on housing without strain and would inflate an area's median burden.
F08.support_span: the top quantile was removed from the final dataset

F09.proposition: The measure follows the US Department of Housing and Urban Development's 30 percent standard, under which a household spending more than 30 percent of income on rent and utilities is counted as cost-burdened.
F09.support_span: This follows HUD's longstanding 30 percent standard

F10.proposition: HUD adopted the 30 percent figure in 1981; earlier public-housing programmes had used 25 percent, and the threshold is traced to a 1969 amendment by Senator Edward Brooke.
F10.support_span: HUD adopted the 30% standard in 1981, evolving from a 25% threshold used in earlier public housing programs

F11.proposition: On a ride around Prospect Park the bike rolled easily along Prospect Park West and then the brake engaged in Windsor Terrace, nearly stopping it.
F11.support_span: Blinder cruised easily down Prospect Park West until he hit Windsor Terrace. Then the brake kicked in, and the bike was nearly frozen.

F12.proposition: Median household income in the community district covering Windsor Terrace and Sunset Park was about $97,000 in 2024, per a NYU Furman Center analysis.
F12.support_span: about $97,000 in 2024, according to an analysis by NYU's Furman Center

F13.proposition: Median asking rent in that area was $2,250 in 2021, when Citi Bike docks arrived, and $3,800 five years later, per StreetEasy - a rise far exceeding inflation.
F13.support_span: the median asking rent was $2,250 ... that figure grew to $3,800, far exceeding the rate of inflation

F14.proposition: Riding near NYCHA public-housing complexes, the device released resistance.
F14.support_span: As Blinder rode near NYCHA complexes in Brooklyn, the device let up some resistance

F15.proposition: Blinder said that easing over public housing shows public housing is working and offsetting the burden, but does not mean residents' lives are more affordable as such.
F15.support_span: it's really just showing that public housing is working ... but it doesn't necessarily mean their lives are more affordable per se

F16.proposition: Areas registering a higher rent burden are often not low-income neighbourhoods but corridors where housing costs have risen rapidly.
F16.support_span: Many areas that have a higher rent burden aren't low-income neighborhoods, but corridors that have seen a rapid rise in housing costs in recent years.

F17.proposition: The ACS is a sample rather than a census, and at block-group level the sample in any one area is small with correspondingly wide margins of error.
F17.support_span: The American Community Survey is a sample, not a census. At the block-group level ... the margins of error are correspondingly wide

F18.proposition: At small geographies an ACS margin of error can exceed the estimate itself; one published example gives an estimate of 28 with a margin of error of plus or minus 33.
F18.support_span: the 2012-2016 ACS 5-Year Estimate for the population of females under 5 years old is 28 with a MOE of +/- 33

F19.proposition: Where a block group's sample is too small or unreliable, the ACS publishes no estimate, and both the device and the map render this as no reading rather than as zero.
F19.support_span: The device and the map both show these as no reading rather than as zero

F20.proposition: Blinder wrote that an absence of data is not an absence of pressure, and that showing it as flat ground would be a lie told by the visualization rather than by the data.
F20.support_span: an absence of data is not an absence of pressure, and rendering it as flat ground would be a lie told by the visualization rather than by the data

F21.proposition: Rent burden does not measure overcrowding, housing quality, eviction risk, informal tenancy, security of a lease, harassment, feelings of safety, or how long a household has been holding on.
F21.support_span: It does not measure overcrowding, housing quality, eviction risk, informal or unrecorded tenancy, the security of a lease, surveillance, harassment, feelings of safety, or how long a household has been holding on.

F22.proposition: The survey covers households, so people with no housing at all are absent from it by construction.
F22.support_span: nothing about people with no housing at all - who are, by construction, absent from a survey of households

F23.proposition: Blinder wrote that the difficulty a rider feels does not translate to the lived experiences and hardships of the people represented in the data.
F23.support_span: That difficulty does not translate to the lived experiences and hardships of those represented in the data.

F24.proposition: Blinder described the work as creating a physical glitch rather than simulating housing insecurity.
F24.support_span: Instead of simulating housing insecurity, Ground Truth creates a physical glitch

F25.proposition: Across dozens of Citi Bikes handled during installation and removal, roughly one in four had a loose front-brake cable that made the front brake ineffective, and Blinder corrected them.
F25.support_span: roughly one in four had a loose front-brake cable that rendered the front brake ineffective. I corrected these issues during the installation and removal process.

F26.proposition: Citi Bike is the largest bike-share system in the United States, is owned and operated by Lyft, and unlike other major US systems receives no public operating subsidy.
F26.support_span: owned and operated by Lyft and, unlike other major U.S. systems, receives no public operating subsidy

F27.proposition: Citi Bike raised prices for five consecutive years; by 2026 annual membership was $239 and a 45-minute e-bike ride could cost a member $12.15, close to three times the 2020 price.
F27.support_span: annual membership had reached $239, while a 45-minute e-bike ride could cost a member $12.15

F28.proposition: Blinder is 41, lost his job during the pandemic and began earning money as a delivery worker, and had the idea then.
F28.support_span: came up with the idea during the pandemic, when he lost his job and started making money as a delivery worker

F29.proposition: Blinder said the experience of moving through the city showed him how much its economic and psychological qualities differed block by block.
F29.support_span: seeing, just how much the, income, economic and psychological qualities of the city differed so much on a block-by-block basis

F30.proposition: The project was funded by a $10,000 award from Idle Hands.
F30.support_span: funded with a $10,000 award from the group Idle Hands

F31.proposition: More than half of New York City residents spend at least 30 percent of income on rent, and about three in ten spend more than half.
F31.support_span: More than half the city's residents spend at least 30% of their income on rent ... About three out of 10 spend more than half

F32.proposition: Blinder built the enclosure on a 3D printer and said he hopes people in other cities with bike-share systems will download the specifications and build their own.
F32.support_span: He made the device on a 3D printer, and said he hopes people in other cities with bike share programs will download the specs
